claude_proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_mode_switch
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The item has six mutually exclusive persistent button states, each entered by a Bonus Action and lasting until another button is pressed or toggled off. The current MagicItemRecord can carry only one mechanics family and has no way to represent item-local mode state with replacement semantics across passive and utility forms.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "You can press one of the following buttons as a Bonus Action; a button's effect lasts until you push a different button or until you push the same button again, which causes the rod to revert to its normal form."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_composite_mechanics
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rod combines always-on weapon bonuses, persistent alternate forms, on-hit optional riders with dawn resets, and a separate Magic action fear ability. The current magic-item surface forces one top-level mechanics family (`passive` or `activation`) and cannot honestly encode a multi-property item with independent triggers and resources.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "It has three other properties as well, detailed below."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: MagicItemMechanics.on_hit_trigger
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Drain Life and Paralyze are optional riders that trigger when the wielder hits with a melee attack using the rod. `on_hit_trigger` exists only for mastery, not for magic items, so these cannot be represented without widening the magic-item mechanics union or introducing composition.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "When you hit a creature with a melee attack using the rod, you can force the target to make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw."
